subject: verify-case.py: unittest timeout from board/config.json (default 900); a timeout ends as unmeasured rc 2, not a traceback
objective: scripts/verify-case.py reads the timeout of its unittest subprocess (red / check / extract all use run_cases) from board/config.json key verify_case.timeout_seconds through one resolver case_timeout(root): key absent -> 900 (todays value), a positive int -> that value, anything else (0, negative, non-int, bool, string) -> one stderr warning naming the key and the bad value, then 900. A run that exceeds the timeout no longer dies on an uncaught subprocess.TimeoutExpired: it ends rc 2 with a stderr reason naming the seconds, the unittest modules and the config key, writes no baseline-red.json and leaves the ticket file byte-identical (same contract as unmeasured()). board/config.json carries the key explicitly (value per outline Q1, recommended 2700) so the cloud container can measure #155 (tests.test_auto_fix as a whole module does not finish in 900 s there).
acceptance: A1 resolver (unit layer, importlib-load scripts/verify-case.py, sandbox root with board/config.json): no verify_case key -> case_timeout(root) == 900; {"verify_case": {"timeout_seconds": 1200}} -> 1200; each of 0, -5, 1.5, "600", true, null -> 900 and stderr contains verify_case.timeout_seconds; unreadable config.json -> 900. Expected values come from this ticket, not from the code.

A2 red times out (CLI layer, CaseSandbox like tests/test_verify_case.py): config timeout_seconds=2, ticket verify.files = one case file whose test does time.sleep(10) then fails -> verify-case.py red <n> --ref <base> --out-dir <d> returns rc 2 within 9 s wall; stderr names 2 seconds, the case module and verify_case.timeout_seconds; stderr has no 'Traceback'; <d> has no baseline-red.json; tickets/<n>.json bytes unchanged.
A3 check times out: same fixture through verify-case.py check <n> --ref <base> --candidate <tree> -> rc 2, same stderr contract, ticket verify.baseline unchanged (bytes of the ticket file unchanged).

A4 within the limit nothing changes: config timeout_seconds=60, a case that sleeps 1 s and fails on an assert -> red behaves exactly as without the key (rc and baseline-red.json content equal to a run with the key absent, compared in the same test).
A5 board/config.json has verify_case.timeout_seconds set to the value ruled in Q1 (recommended 2700); every other key of board/config.json is unchanged (diff of board/config.json is that one key).
A6 existing tests/test_verify_case.py cases stay green unchanged (no edits to existing cases; oracle checked: tests/test_verify_case.py has no TIMEOUT / 900 assertion, grep at 7fd9894).
test_plan: Worker runs only, foreground: timeout 580 python3 -m unittest tests.test_verify_case <verifier case module if separate>; report Ran/OK verbatim. No full suite, no test_auto_fix (that is what times out). Verifier writes cases for A1-A4 in tests/ (verify.tags stays empty, agent-control rule #29). Mutations (worker, optional, not measured by opener): (m1) keep TIMEOUT = 900 and ignore config -> A2 red (sleep 10 completes, rc != 2); (m2) drop the TimeoutExpired handling -> A2 red (Traceback in stderr); (m3) accept bool true as 1 -> A1 red.
outline: Why: #155 verifier r1 OBJECTION (blocking, deferred to this ticket): verify-case.py:97 TIMEOUT=900 hard-coded; run_cases runs whole modules; tests.test_auto_fix+test_agent_cost_hook+test_ticket hit TimeoutExpired after 900 s in the cloud, so red and the gate check cannot measure #155.
